title: VALOR Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on November 7, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Veterans Apprenticeship and Labor Opportunity Reform Act or the VALOR Act

(Sec. 2) This bill provides that the state approving agency for a multi-state non-federal apprenticeship program is: (1) for program approval purposes, the state approving agency for the state in which the headquarters of the apprenticeship program is located; and (2) for all other purposes, the state approving agency for the state in which the apprenticeship program takes place.

(Sec. 3) The bill eliminates the requirement that the veteran or other eligible person enrolled in an apprenticeship or other on-job training program must certify such person's program attendance to receive a training assistance allowance.

summary.headline: This 2017 law changes how multi-state apprenticeship programs are approved and removes an attendance-certification step for veterans who receive training allowances.
summary.what_it_does: For multi-state apprenticeship programs that are not run by the federal government, the state approving agency that handles program approval is the one in the state where the program's headquarters is located. For all other purposes, the agency in the state where the program takes place handles oversight. The law also removes the requirement that veterans and other eligible people in apprenticeship or on-the-job training programs certify their attendance to receive the training assistance allowance.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans enrolled in apprenticeship or on-the-job training programs
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to certify their program attendance to receive the training assistance allowance.

who_it_affects.group: Other eligible people enrolled in apprenticeship or on-the-job training programs
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to certify their program attendance to receive the training assistance allowance.

who_it_affects.group: Operators of multi-state non-federal apprenticeship programs
who_it_affects.how: Program approval is handled by the state agency where the program's headquarters is located, while other matters go to the agency in each state where the program takes place.
They take on defined roles for multi-state apprenticeship programs based on headquarters location for approval and program location for other purposes.
